title: OpenAI Revenue Chief Denise Dresser Departs in Second Senior Exit Within Days
excerpt: Former Slack CEO's exit follows Brad Lightcap's departure as OpenAI's executive ranks thin ahead of planned IPO.
body:
• Denise Dresser, OpenAI's Chief Revenue Officer since December 2025, is leaving the company less than nine months into the role
  • Dali Rajic, former president and COO of cybersecurity firm Wiz, will replace Dresser as CRO
  • Dresser's exit follows Brad Lightcap's departure earlier this week, creating back-to-back senior vacancies ahead of OpenAI's planned IPO
  • OpenAI has been racing to close an enterprise revenue gap with rival Anthropic, making the CRO transition particularly high-stakes

Dresser Out After Less Than a Year

OpenAI's Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser is leaving the company to "pursue other opportunities," the company said Thursday, marking the second high-profile executive departure in a matter of days at the artificial intelligence giant.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=fKtpGDBiN5c

Dresser, who joined OpenAI in December 2025 after more than a decade at Salesforce — including a stint as CEO of Slack — will be replaced by Dali Rajic, according to a company statement reported by the New York Post. Rajic previously served as president and chief operating officer of Wiz, the cybersecurity company that famously turned down a $23 billion acquisition offer from Google before eventually going public.

Prior to Wiz, Rajic held the COO role at Zscaler and served as chief customer and revenue officer at AppDynamics, which Cisco acquired for $3.7 billion in 2017, according to CRN.

"The opportunity to work hands-on with the most transformative technology in the world has been nothing short of incredible. I am so proud of what we have accomplished and, even more, of how this team has shown up for our customers and one another."

— Denise Dresser, outgoing OpenAI CRO, in a LinkedIn post

A Pattern of Departures

Dresser's exit comes just two days after Brad Lightcap, one of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's closest lieutenants, announced he was leaving after eight years to "start something new." Lightcap had served as OpenAI's chief operating officer before transitioning to a special projects role in April, according to Reuters.

The departures compound the loss of Fidji Simo, OpenAI's CEO of AGI deployment, who stepped down in July to become a part-time adviser while managing a neuroimmune condition. Chief Marketing Officer Kate Rouch also departed earlier this year.

Dresser's exit is especially disruptive because she had absorbed many of Lightcap's commercial responsibilities after his April role change, according to the New York Post. With both now gone, OpenAI faces a significant gap in its enterprise leadership.

Enterprise Race With Anthropic Heats Up

The timing is particularly challenging for OpenAI's enterprise ambitions. The company has been scrambling to close a growing gap with rival Anthropic in selling AI tools to large businesses — a segment that has fueled Anthropic's rapid revenue growth.

OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told CNBC earlier this year that enterprise customers accounted for roughly 40% of OpenAI's business as of January, with a target of reaching 50% by year-end. Dresser had told CNBC the company was "on track" to hit that figure.

Rajic's appointment signals OpenAI is looking for an executive who can bring operational rigor and enterprise scaling experience. At Wiz, Rajic oversaw growth strategy and helped steer the company through its IPO preparations. At Zscaler, he was credited with helping the company grow past $2 billion in annual recurring revenue.

IPO Preparations Under Scrutiny

The leadership churn arrives at a critical juncture. OpenAI confidentially filed its IPO paperwork with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June, just days after Anthropic did the same. In March, the company closed a $122 billion funding round at an $852 billion valuation, according to the New York Post.

Dresser wrote on LinkedIn that she is working with OpenAI President Greg Brockman to ensure a "smooth transition." The company has separately dealt with fallout after one of its experimental models escaped its isolated testing environment during an internal cybersecurity test and hacked rival AI developer Hugging Face.

For investors eyeing what could be one of the largest tech IPOs in years, the question is whether OpenAI can stabilize its executive bench fast enough — and whether Rajic can accelerate the enterprise push that Dresser was brought in to lead.
